learning_outcomes.text: Recognize and understand the basic principles of thermodynamics and heat transfer (conduction, convection, and radiation) that apply to solving real engineering installation problems.
Apply the basic principles of thermodynamics and heat transfer (conduction, convection, and radiation) that apply to solving real engineering installation problems.
Apply the basic principles of fluid mechanics in solving real engineering installation problems (calculation of pipes, channels, and fluid systems).
Recognize and understand the basic principles of fluid mechanics that apply to engineering.
Recognize and understand the training needs that will be useful for successfully solving new situations related to industrial engineering.
Project in the field of industrial technical engineering.
Develop projects in the field of industrial technical engineering.
Direct projects in the field of industrial technical engineering.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Develop measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task plans and other works typical of the field of technical engineering.
Recognize and understand the legislation necessary for the exercise of the profession of industrial technical engineer.
Apply knowledge typical of industrial engineering in learning new methods and theories.
Show the advantages and opportunities of different solutions to the same problem in a critical and constructive way.
Correctly and pertinently use mandatory specifications, regulations, and standards.
Apply the appropriate legislation to the exercise of the profession of industrial technical engineer.

syllabus_topics: TOPIC 1: INTRODUCTION AND FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS: Closed and open systems, System properties, Temperature and pressure.
TOPIC 2: ENERGY AND ENERGY TRANSFER: Heat and work, First Law of Thermodynamics, Energy balance in closed systems.
TOPIC 3: THERMODYNAMIC PROPERTIES OF PURE SUBSTANCES: Phase changes, Properties of gases, Equations of state, Enthalpy, internal energy, and specific heats.
TOPIC 4: ENERGY ANALYSIS AND BALANCES IN OPEN SYSTEMS: Conservation of mass, Flow work and energy of a moving fluid, Energy analysis of steady-flow systems.
TOPIC 5: SECOND LAW OF THERMODYNAMICS: Reversible and irreversible processes, Heat engines, refrigerators and heat pumps, Carnot cycle, Entropy.
TOPIC 6: THERMODYNAMIC CYCLES: Gas and vapor power cycles, Refrigeration cycles.
TOPIC 1: INTRODUCTION AND FUNDAMENTAL CONCEPTS: Continuum hypothesis, Density and specific gravity, Surface tension and vapor pressure, Viscosity. Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids.
TOPIC 2: FLUID STATICS: Fundamental equation of hydrostatics, Buoyancy. Archimedes' Principle, Forces on walls or gates.
TOPIC 3: FLUID DYNAMICS: Continuity equation, Bernoulli's equation, Torricelli's Theorem, Flow rate measurement.
TOPIC 5: PIPE ANALYSIS: Laminar and turbulent flow, Reynolds number, Types of losses.

assessment_methods.method: Mixed tests (two written exams, one for Block I and one for Block II)
Continuous assessment (active attendance, participation, in-class problem-solving, online questionnaires, presentations, and/or reports)
Assignments (written or practical activities, individual or group, with or without oral defense, including laboratory reports)

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a 70% weight for mixed tests, 15% for continuous assessment, and 15% for assignments. The mixed tests consist of two written exams, one covering Block I and the other covering Block II. Continuous assessment involves active participation and various tasks throughout the course. Assignments include written or practical activities, often evaluated through written reports for laboratory sessions. No specific minimum marks for components or overall and no resit arrangements are stated in the syllabus.
